scenario: Indian brands Dolo 650 and Crocin (both paracetamol) taken together

segments.speaker: DOCTOR
segments.text: What are you taking for the fever?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I have fever. I took Dolo 650 in the morning and Crocin at night.

notes: REVIEW_REQUIRED is the policy outcome: the drug was found by the LLM only, never by the deterministic lexicon. No rule models same-generic duplication.

scenario: Reaction-as-allergy: Augmentin caused face swelling + breathing trouble; cefuroxime prescribed

segments.speaker: DOCTOR
segments.text: Have you had any reaction to antibiotics before?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Last year I took Augmentin and my face swelled up and I had trouble breathing.

segments.speaker: DOCTOR
segments.text: Thank you. For your ear infection I will prescribe cefuroxime 250 mg twice a day.

notes: Ground truth: the swelling / breathing trouble are the past reaction, not current symptoms, and Augmentin is not a current medication. The rule extractor labels both wrongly and merge never removes rule entities (rules win), so hybrid keeps two false-positive entities AND the safety engine raises a spurious BLOCKED MEDICATION_ALLERGY on the rule-labelled CURRENT Augmentin. Achievable hybrid status is therefore CONFLICT_DETECTED (over-triage, safe direction).

scenario: Lay terms: tummy hurting, giddy, loose motions

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: My tummy has been hurting since yesterday, I feel giddy and I have loose motions.

scenario: Double negation: 'I can't deny the cough has been bad'

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can't deny the cough has been bad this week.

notes: The rule extractor reads this as cough ABSENT and rules win on disagreement, so the best achievable hybrid outcome is REVIEW_REQUIRED (rule/LLM disagreement), not SAFE.

segments.speaker: DOCTOR
segments.text: This is a 4-year-old boy and he weighs 15 kg. He has a fever and ear pain.

segments.speaker: DOCTOR
segments.text: I will prescribe codeine syrup and ibuprofen 600 mg twice a day.

notes: Clinically, ibuprofen 600 mg for 15 kg (~40 mg/kg) is also an overdose, but the safety engine has adult max doses only (no weight-based rule), so that conflict is not in expected.conflicts.
